faq.a: The trachea, or windpipe, is the tube that carries air from your throat to your lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage stop it collapsing, and its lining has mucus and tiny hairs to trap and sweep away dirt.
The trachea splits into two bronchi, one going into each lung. These branch into thousands of smaller tubes called bronchioles, which end in the alveoli.
Alveoli are tiny air sacs at the ends of the bronchioles, covered in capillaries. Oxygen diffuses from them into the blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses out of the blood into them.
The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. When it contracts it flattens, making the chest bigger, so air is drawn in. When it relaxes, air is pushed out.

faq.q: Why do we breathe through the nose?
faq.a: The nose warms and moistens the air, and its hairs and mucus trap dust and germs before they reach the lungs.
asks: Is it better to breathe through your nose?

facts: Human lungs contain roughly 300 to 500 million alveoli.
The trachea is held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage.

quiz.say: Which order does air pass through?
quiz.show: Which order does air pass through?
quiz.why: Air goes down the trachea, into a bronchus, through smaller bronchioles and into the alveoli.

wrong.1: This starts at the deepest point; air starts at the trachea.
wrong.2: The trachea comes before the bronchi, and bronchioles before alveoli.

quiz.say: What happens when the diaphragm contracts?
quiz.show: What happens when the diaphragm contracts?

options.show: It flattens and air is drawn in
options.say: It flattens and air is drawn in

options.show: It domes up and air is pushed out
options.say: It domes up and air is pushed out

quiz.why: Contracting flattens the diaphragm, making the chest bigger, so air flows in.

wrong.1: That happens when the diaphragm relaxes.
wrong.2: The diaphragm moves air; it does not control the heart.
